short: Irish republicans launched an armed insurrection against British rule in Ireland while the UK was engaged in the First World War.
full:
On 24 April 1916, members of the Irish Volunteers and the Irish Citizen Army seized key locations in Dublin and proclaimed an independent Irish Republic. The rebellion, centered at the General Post Office, caught the British authorities by surprise but suffered from a lack of popular support and overwhelming military disparity.

The British army suppressed the uprising by 29 April, devastating parts of central Dublin with artillery fire. Although the rising itself was a military failure, the subsequent execution of its leaders by British authorities drastically shifted Irish public opinion. The perceived martyrdom of the rebel leaders catalyzed support for Sinn Féin and led directly to the Irish War of Independence three years later.
